title: Rice Varieties in the Philippines: Inbreds, Hybrids and Special Rice
metaTitle: Rice Varieties in the Philippines: NSIC List and Hybrids
metaDescription: Compare rice varieties in the Philippines: NSIC Rc 216, Rc 222 and Rc 402, hybrids like SL 8H and Jackpot 102, Jasponica rice and the store brands.
keywords: variety of rice in the philippines
kinds of rice in the philippines
excerpt: The NSIC has approved a long list of rice varieties in the Philippines, but most farms plant only a handful. This guide compares the popular NSIC inbreds, the main hybrids, special rice like Jasponica and the store brands you see at the market. Maturity and yield figures come from PhilRice and the seed companies.

heroImage.alt: Palay heads filling out in a green rice field

blocks.text: A rice variety, or rice breed as some farmers call it, is a line of rice with fixed traits. It sets how tall the plant grows, how many days it needs, how the rice tastes and which pests it tolerates. The right choice can add sacks per hectare. But the wrong one can lose a season to a typhoon or a planthopper outbreak. That is why no single variety of rice in the Philippines wins in every town.
Kinds of rice in the Philippines
Most seed you can buy falls into three groups.

items: **Inbred rice.** Varieties such as NSIC Rc 216 and Rc 222. If the crop is pure, you can save seed for next season after a germination test.

**Hybrid rice.** First generation (F1) seed from two parent lines, such as SL 8H or Jackpot 102. A rice hybrid has higher yield potential, but saved grain does not grow true to type, so you buy new seed every season.
**Special rice.** Aromatic, glutinous (malagkit), japonica and pigmented rice, grown for taste and a higher price.

blocks.text: PhilRice also gives its inbreds local names by environment. For example, Tubigan varieties suit irrigated lowland, while Sahod Ulan varieties suit rainfed lowland. Its Binhing Palay app lets you search registered varieties and their traits, so it works as a Philippine rice variety list in your pocket.
Popular rice varieties in the Philippines: the inbreds
These are the inbreds farmers ask about most. The figures come from PhilRice trials across many sites, so your own field may do better or worse.

blocks.caption: Popular NSIC inbreds from PhilRice data (t/ha means tonnes per hectare)

blocks.text: Rice variety 216 (NSIC Rc 216, Tubigan 17)

PhilRice calls Rc 216 early maturing, at 112 days transplanted and 104 days direct seeded. In PhilRice trials it averaged 6.0 t/ha transplanted, with a top yield of 9.7 t/ha. It is moderately resistant to brown planthopper, green leafhopper and yellow stem borer. Still, PhilRice rates it susceptible to blast, so scout for blast closely.
Rice variety 222 (NSIC Rc 222, Tubigan 18)

Rc 222 was bred by IRRI and is now one of the most planted inbreds. It matures in 114 days transplanted and 106 days direct seeded. It averaged 6.1 t/ha transplanted, up to 10.0 t/ha. PhilRice notes a yield edge in the wet season and good adaptation to both irrigated and rainfed fields. That is why PalayCheck recommends it for both seasons in Central Luzon.
NSIC Rc 402: rice variety characteristics

PhilRice released Rc 402 in 2015 and recommends it for direct seeding in Luzon. It averages 5.5 t/ha and matures in 107 days direct seeded, or 114 days transplanted. The plant stands about 95 cm tall. Its grain is medium, milling recovery reached 69.3 percent in trials, and the cooked rice is moderately soft.
Rice hybrid varieties

A rice hybrid costs more per kilo of seed, but you plant less of it. PalayCheck even advises a lower seeding rate for hybrids in mechanical transplanting because the seed is expensive.

At a 2023 DA Bicol field day, nine seed companies showed their hybrids to farmers. With good weather, management and fertilizer, they said, these can reach up to 14 tonnes per hectare. Maturity ranged from 104 to 118 days after sowing. Those are best case numbers, so compare them with your own records.
SL Agritech Corporation and SL 8H

SL Agritech Corporation (SLAC) is a private company that breeds, produces and sells hybrid rice seed and premium rice. Its best known hybrid is SL 8H. For SL 8H the company lists 7 to 17 t/ha, 105 to 115 days to maturity, 118 cm plant height and 12 to 28 productive tillers. SLAC also says SL 8H shatters little, so you can harvest it up to 90 percent grain maturity. Those are company claims, so test them on your own lot.
Jackpot 102 and other hybrids

Jackpot 102, registered as NSIC Rc 666H, comes from Leads Agri Ventures, which calls it its first hybrid seed, introduced in 2019. We found no official figure for the Jackpot rice variety maturity. The DA Bicol report gives one range, 104 to 118 days after sowing, for all the hybrids shown at the field day, so it is not a number for Jackpot alone. Read the days to maturity on the seed bag, or ask your dealer, before you date your season.

Other hybrids at the same field day included Bigante Plus and Habilis Plus from Bayer and TH82 from SeedWorks. There were also NK 5017 from Syngenta, LP 2096 from LongPing and Mestizo 30 from Allied Botanical.

blocks.title: Brochure yields versus farm averages
blocks.text: Seed company yields usually describe best case fields. For scale, the PSA put the national average palay yield at 4.14 tonnes per hectare in 2025. So compare any new variety with your own last seasons, not with a brochure.
Special rice: Jasponica rice and japonica

Jasponica rice comes from SL Agritech, which describes it as a cross of Thai jasmine rice and Japanese rice. It is sold as premium milled rice under the Doña Maria brand, named after the mother of chairman Henry Lim. A 2011 Philstar report described the cooked grain as soft, sticky and chewy, with an aroma. Treat that as the company's description, since we found no PhilRice trial data for it.

For a true japonica, PhilRice announced NSIC Rc 414, named Japonica 4, in 2016. Aromatic and glutinous types, like the malagkit used for kakanin, also belong to special rice.
Rice brands in the Philippines are not varieties

Walk into any public market and you will see names like Sinandomeng or Dinorado on the rice box. PhilRice calls these popular rice brands. In 2018 the NFA limited local rice labels to four classes: regular milled, well milled, premium and special rice. The rule replaced brand names like Sinandomeng and Dinorado, although a 2021 PhilRice brief found some retailers still use them.

Company brands, such as Doña Maria from SL Agritech Corporation, are a different thing. They tell you who packed the rice. But the seed you plant should carry an NSIC name on a certified tag, so when a buyer asks what you planted, answer with the variety.
How to choose the right rice variety
PalayCheck gives four tests for choosing a rice variety in the Philippines, plus one habit.

items: It suits your environment and season: irrigated or rainfed, dry or wet season.
It answers your local problem. In typhoon areas, pick a maturity that lets the crop escape the worst months.
It did well in at least two seasons of adaptability trials by PhilRice or your DA office.
Your buyer or miller wants it.
Rotate varieties every 2 to 4 croppings, which PalayCheck advises as part of pest management.

blocks.text: Questions about rice varieties in the Philippines

items.q: What is the best rice variety in the Philippines?
items.a: There is no single best one. PalayCheck advises a variety that suits your environment and season, answers your local problem, did well in two seasons of local trials and sells well. In Central Luzon, for example, PalayCheck recommends NSIC Rc 222 for both seasons.

items.q: How many days is NSIC Rc 216?
items.a: PhilRice lists 112 days after sowing when transplanted and 104 days when direct seeded. It averaged 6.0 t/ha transplanted in PhilRice trials.

We found no official maturity figure for Jackpot 102. A DA Bicol report on the 2023 field day gave one range, 104 to 118 days after sowing, for all the hybrids shown, Jackpot 102 among them. Check the seed bag or ask your dealer.

items.q: Can I save seed from a hybrid crop?
items.a: No. Hybrid seed is first generation, and grain saved from it does not grow true to type. So buy new certified hybrid seed every season. You can save seed from a pure inbred crop if it passes a germination test.
Jasponica is SL Agritech's own rice, sold as premium milled rice under its Doña Maria brand. The company describes it as a cross of Thai jasmine rice and Japanese rice.
